terms.name: shared interface / phreatic head
terms.definition: One physical groundwater/interface head when SWAP and MODFLOW represent the same phreatic state rather than two states separated by a finite resistance.
terms.caution: A shared head is not a complete SWAP state when internal unsaturated memory exists (DSW11/DSW15).

terms.name: whole-column physical storage change
terms.definition: Change in water stored in the SWAP control volume over the coupling window.
terms.caution: MAP03 identifies J_S≈u only in the simple drainage-free fixture; this is not a universal definition of u.

terms.name: accepted physical bottom outward exchange
terms.definition: Signed whole-window bottom exchange from the real SWAP corrector; q_swap is its rate representation used by the coupling residual and the committed interface ledger.
terms.derivative: J_R=dE_bottom/dH or the corresponding rate derivative
terms.caution: In the simple fixture J_R≈-J_S because all other balance terms are head-independent; this sign relation is process-specific.

terms.name: non-bottom process remainder
terms.definition: Atmospheric, root, drainage and other non-bottom terms required to close the SWAP water balance.
terms.caution: A head-dependent B_nonbottom breaks the simple J_S≈-J_R alias and is the target of MAP09+ follow-up.

terms.name: accepted-trajectory predictor response coefficient
terms.production_definition: u=dt/(dH_bot/dq_bot) along the accepted qbot-controlled predictor trajectory
terms.caution: u can coincide with storage sensitivity in a restricted fixture, but its production authority is the inverse finite-window qbot-to-head response, not a universal physical-storage declaration.

terms.name: historical predictor response quantity
terms.caution: Its total derivative across neighboring predictor trajectories is not +u/dt because q_bot and potentially u change with the trajectory.

terms.symbol: partial q_u / partial H | predictor frozen
terms.name: production affine response slope
terms.production_definition: +u/dt with predictor u and q_bot held fixed; cell response is reanchored by changing the intercept after real-SWAP corrector observations.
terms.caution: Do not call this the total physical derivative of q_u, bottom exchange, or a physical interface conductance.

terms.name: reanchored affine groundwater-facing response
terms.definition: q_ref+slope*(H-H_ref); after a rejected coupling iterate, the line is reanchored through the measured real-SWAP corrector point while the chosen slope policy is retained.
terms.caution: Different slopes may share the same accepted physical fixed point but take different paths through the corrector admissibility domain.

terms.name: MODFLOW API affine representation
terms.definition: Q=HCOF*H-RHS after area/time/unit transformation of the selected affine response.
terms.caution: Dimensional similarity to storage/time or conductance does not establish physical ownership.

terms.name: finite-resistance interface conductance
terms.definition: q=C_link*(h_1-h_2) for two physically distinct states separated by a represented resistance.
terms.caution: Not interchangeable with u, HCOF, or a shared-state storage response.

terms.name: solver/Jacobian derivative
terms.definition: Derivative used to solve the currently assembled residual; may include storage, process tangents and/or affine coupling terms.
terms.caution: Solver convergence and physical correctness/mass closure are separate acceptance objects (DSW05, DSW19).

synthesis: DSW01-DSW20 establish the transparent algebraic signatures of shared storage, duplicate storage, finite resistance, sinks, internal memory, aggregation and converged-but-wrong coupling.
MAP03 shows that in a simple real-Richards fixture u matches whole-column storage sensitivity while the physical bottom exchange has the opposite head sensitivity.
MAP07 shows that +u/dt is a partial affine-extension derivative; along the E4 predictor family the total historical q_u derivative is about one millionth of that slope on the fixed B3 plateau points.
MAP04 shows slope policy is practically irrelevant to accepted physics in an easy short-window case.
MAP05 falsifies universal slope-policy invariance: intercept-only changes the path enough to hit a corrector-domain failure in B3.

MAP05A shows the independently measured negative corrector slope J_R is nevertheless admissible and reaches essentially the same B3 accepted head, flux and ledger as current +u in the same three outer iterations.
MAP06 shows why path matters: the B3 prescribed-head corrector admissibility set is deterministic but fragmented on the preregistered picometre grid.
current_contract_interpretation: Accepted physical exchange authority is the real-SWAP corrector plus committed whole-window interface ledger.
The production +u/dt line is best described, on current evidence, as an iteration-response surrogate constructed from accepted predictor sensitivity and reanchored to physical corrector observations.
Current evidence does not justify describing +u/dt as a physical exchange conductance or as the total derivative of historical q_u.

Current evidence also does not justify declaring the production coupling defective: the accepted physical state is separately certified by corrector residual and ledger, and both +u and J_R policies can reach the same fixed point in B3.
unresolved: How does the decomposition change when a head/state-dependent non-bottom process contributes materially to the real-SWAP window balance?
Which slope policy is most robust across a prospectively defined family of admitted corrector domains without compromising accepted physics?
What precise historical/SIMGRO contract motivated freezing q_bot in the affine extension, and should that semantic intent be documented explicitly?
forbidden_inference: No production source change is authorized by this taxonomy.
No universal ranking of +u, zero slope or J_R is supported.
Do not infer a physical q-link unless two physical heads and a resistance law exist.
Do not infer that shared head eliminates internal SWAP memory/state.
